commits.edited_message:
don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

* don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests

Also reject a declared ChannelGroupsManifests count that could not
possibly be backed by the remaining data, using a small helper
(haveBytes()) rather than trusting the raw entry count on its own.

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

* modify _manifest in place to avoid chance of unnecessary copy

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

---------

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
Co-authored-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read (#2572)

A single unvalidated 64-bit `_uncompressedDataSize` field, read directly
from an EXR file's `idManifest` attribute, was used as a `std::vector`
allocation size in `IDManifest::IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)`
before decompression and before any consistency check. Depending on the
value an attacker writes into that field, an application that reads ID
manifests can be forced to either exhaust memory (an uncatchable SIGKILL,
since the vector's value-initialization physically dirties every page)
or dereference a null pointer, because a declared size of 0 makes
`uncomp.data()` null while the length check that follows decompression
still passes (0 == 0). Declared sizes of 1-3 instead produce a silent
heap out-of-bounds read of the version field. All of this is reachable
from a 343-byte file through the public, non-explicit, IMF_EXPORT
constructors `IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)` and
`IDManifest(const char*, const char*)`.

Two independent checks are added, since either alone leaves the other
failure mode reachable:

- In the `CompressedIDManifest` constructor, reject the declared
  uncompressed size before allocating anything for it if it is zero, or
  exceeds the compressed size scaled by zlib's maximum expansion ratio
  (~1032:1) -- tying the claim to bytes that must actually be present in
  the file, rather than trusting an arbitrary 64-bit value. This does
  *not* impose an absolute size ceiling: OpenEXR places no fixed limit
  on data size by default (see `Header::setMaxImageSize()`, which is
  off/unlimited unless an application opts in), so a legitimate manifest
  may be arbitrarily large provided the file actually contains that much
  compressed data.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, bounds-check the 4-byte version field read
  against the end of the buffer, reusing the `haveBytes()` helper that
  the ChannelGroupsManifests count check already relies on, exactly as
  the adjacent `readStringList()` already does for its own reads. This
  is the fix that actually matters for the null/overread cases, since
  `init()` is reachable directly through the public `IDManifest(const
  char*, const char*)` constructor without ever passing through the size
  check above.

Also replaced `&uncomp[0]` with `uncomp.data()`, which is well-defined
for an empty vector.

Verified by regenerating the reporter's PoC files (declared sizes of
512 MiB, 0, and 1) against `exrmanifest`: all are now rejected with a
clean exception instead of crashing or being killed by the OOM killer.
Also verified that a legitimate, honestly-compressed 300 MB manifest is
still accepted. The existing `testIDManifest` suite, which round-trips
legitimate manifests up to ~44 MB decoded, continues to pass.

Assisted-by: GitHub Copilot CLI (model: Claude Sonnet 5)

Addresses https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr/security/advisories/GHSA-5j5m-22wr-mhc6

Signed-off-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

coupling: Both edited commits touch IDManifest::init() in src/lib/OpenEXR/ImfIDManifest.cpp. d6f75dc ("don't preallocate _manifest...") additionally introduces a small helper, haveBytes(data,endOfData,n), used only to extend its own (already-non-exploitable) sanity check on the attacker-controlled ChannelGroupsManifests count; a correct check needs 'data + n <= endOfData', but haveBytes computes 'data + n - 1 <= endOfData', i.e. it is permissive by exactly one byte. In d6f75dc alone this is unobservable: the count check is a loose anti-DoS bound, not the memory-safety guard for any read (each field read inside the manifestEntries loop already has its own independent endOfData-relative bounds check), so no input can turn the one-byte slack into a demonstrable failure using only d6f75dc's code paths. 38d9cbf ("Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read") is a later, chronologically-separate commit that reuses the SAME helper -- introduced one commit earlier -- to express its own new version-field bound: 'if (! haveBytes(data, endOfData, sizeof(unsigned int))) throw'. Here the helper's off-by-one is safety-critical: haveBytes(data,endOfData,4) returns true even when only 3 bytes remain (data+3 <= endOfData), so the check wrongly passes and the subsequent 'Xdr::read<CharPtrIO>(data, version)' reads 4 bytes from a 3-byte-remaining buffer, a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow READ. 38d9cbf's own diff looks correct in isolation: it calls a plausibly-named helper exactly the way the adjacent, already-correct readStringList() bounds its own reads, and the helper's definition (and the one place its flaw is harmless) lives in a different commit. A correct fix must either (a) see both use sites and realize n=sizeof(unsigned int) is safety-critical while n=manifestEntries is not, and fix the shared helper's comparison, or (b) independently re-derive a correct bound at the 38d9cbf call site -- in neither case does patching only one commit's visible diff, taken at face value, reveal the defect: d6f75dc's own code never fails because of it, and 38d9cbf's diff contains no arithmetic to inspect at all.
